name: Unifi UP reward manager accepts a caller-supplied fake pool for LP reward eligibility and reward math
summary: Unifi's UP reward manager 0x5d8aa155 treated any contract whose token0() returned WBNB as a pool in mintUP, and claimUP sized the payout from balanceOf and totalSupply read from that same address. The attacker's fake pool minted UP with 0.001 flash-borrowed BNB, reported a huge LP balance to claim the manager's UP reward reserve, and redeemed the UP for BNB.
notes: Direct unverified runtime with no delegation; its only admin transaction is transferOwnership and eligibility is decided by runtime code (token0() == WBNB), so deployment is the age basis.

Every mint event of the manager since deployment (66,608) names a UnifiRouter-created pool except the anchor's and one copycat's fake pool, created by a different EOA with the same bytecode three days later; it took the dust minted since.

UP has no market price: the manager's net UP outflow (attacker's own minted UP excluded) is valued at the anchor's redemption rate, 10.479279 BNB per UP, times DefiLlama's WBNB price at each transaction.
